Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

lagprotest 0.3.0

  • New period argument in lagged_protest(): when the seasonal cycle does not divide the series length, both series are truncated to their first floor(n / period) * period rows, so that the phase and cyclic schemes, which treat the series as periodic with period n, remain calibrated. In simulations (24–48 time points, cycle of 0.75 n), this brought the Type I error of the global p-value from 0.46–0.94 back to 0.04–0.05 for AR(1) noise of 0.3. Removing the seasonal component by harmonic regression was also tested and left the test liberal, so it was not added.

lagprotest 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • The default permutation scheme is now permutation = "phase" (phase-randomized surrogates), which retains power for the global p-value across lags. Use permutation = "cyclic" for the previous behavior; the phase scheme is random, so set seed for reproducible results.

  • lagged_protest() now defaults to p.adjust.method = "none", because corrections such as Holm are often unattainable with the few permutations of the cyclic scheme. $p.value is now the raw p-value at the optimal lag; the adjusted value is in the new $p.adjusted element, and the number of permutations in $n_perm. print() warns when p-values are unadjusted.

New features

  • lagged_protest() returns a global p-value, $p.global, for the scan across lags. It is a max-statistic test that compares the observed minimum m² across lags with the minimum across lags under each permutation, and so accounts for testing several lags and selecting the optimal one. print() reports it below the optimal lag. Simulations showed that the raw p-value at the optimal lag rejects 10–28% of the time (21–25% on average) when the series are independent.
  • New scheme permutation = "phase": phase-randomized surrogates of Y that keep the amplitude spectrum of each column and the cross-spectra among columns. Unlike cyclic shifts, surrogates do not reproduce the observed alignment at other lags, so the global p-value keeps its power.
  • p.adjust.method = "maxT" gives single-step max-statistic adjusted p-values per lag.
  • permutation = "free" now applies each permutation jointly to all lags, as the max-statistic requires.

Infrastructure

  • Continuous integration: R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu, and test coverage reporting, via GitHub Actions.
  • Spell check of the documentation, contributing guide, code of conduct and issue templates.
  • The vignette now uses US English spelling.

lagprotest 0.1.0

First public release.

  • lagged_protest() scans Procrustes concordance between two ordered multivariate series across candidate lags and tests each lag by permutation. Two schemes are available: cyclic shifts of the full series, optionally with time reversal (default), and free row permutation as in vegan::protest(). P-values are adjusted across lags. Accepts matrices, data frames or dist objects (converted by PCoA).
  • print(), summary(), plot() and residuals() methods for the lag profile, the optimal lag and per-observation Procrustes residuals.
  • simulate_lagged_series() generates seasonal series with AR(1) noise and a known lag, for calibration and power studies.
